test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 13 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution:
Here the correct answer is He had.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to **fill in the blank No. 2** is: **he had.**
 
• In the context of the sentence, the past tense form "he had" is the correct option. It indicates that something had already happened in the past.
 
• The sentence is describing events that occurred in Krishna's life, and the use of the past tense is consistent with the narrative.
 
 
• Example: "He had been born in a small village."
 
• In this example, "had been born" indicates that the person's birth had already taken place in the past.
 
 
 
• In summary, the most appropriate option to** fill in the blank No. 2** is **"he had"** as it correctly conveys that the events being described had already taken place in the past.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other options:
 
• **he have**: This option is not grammatically correct. The correct form should be "he has" in the present tense or "he had" in the past tense.
 
 
• Example: Incorrect - "He have arrived yesterday."
 
• Correct - "He has arrived yesterday." (present tense)
 
• Correct - "He had arrived yesterday." (past tense)
 
 
 
• **he was**: This option is in the past tense, but it does not convey the sense of past events that had already occurred. It implies a continuous action or state in the past.
 
 
• Example: "He was playing soccer when I saw him."
 
• In this example, "was playing" indicates an ongoing action in the past.
 
 
 
• **he has**: This option is in the present tense, which is not suitable for the context of the sentence. The events described in the passage have already happened in the past.
 
 
• Example: "He has a car." (present tense)
 
• In this example, "has" indicates the possession of a car in the present.
